newsitem.title: BERMUDA: Bermuda premier resigns after McDonald's flap.
newsitem.headline: Bermuda premier resigns after McDonald's flap.

text.p: Premier Dr. David Saul, plagued by his decision to allow a former premier to operate McDonald's Corp fast-food restaurants in the British colony, announced on Wednesday that he would resign.
"My retirement from politics ought not to come as any great surprise to those who have studied my career," a grim-faced Saul said at a news conference, reading from a prepared statement.
Saul, premier since August 1995, said he would leave office on March 27 but gave no specific reason for his decision.
Political observers said he would have had difficulty leading his ruling United Bermuda Party (UBP) to victory in the next general election, due to be held by October 1998.
Political observers described Saul's 17 months as premier as lackluster and said his decision to allow McDonald's fast-food restaurants here created an uproar among islanders and in his own party.

Saul said a series of recent opinion polls indicated that his party could have won an election but the margin of victory would have been narrow, confirming his own belief that "now is the right time" to resign. No obvious successor had emerged.

Strenuous oppositon by rebel members of his own party pushed through House of Assembly a bill called the "Prohibited Restaurant Bill," banning McDonald's and other fast-food restaurants from the island.
